transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-01-24 15:00 PST
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Brooks (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (StratoSearch Head of Search), Marcus Hale (Staff ML Eng), Priya Subramanian (PM)

Summary: quick discovery to decide whether to run pilot on Redwood Hosted or go straight to Dedicated/Private. Focus on embeddings dimensions, rerank latency budget, vector DB integration points and throughput.

00:00 - Ethan Brooks: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro - I'm Ethan, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya our solutions engineer.
00:12 - Lina Torres: Hi all, Lina here. We're trying to decide hosting - we have a data residency requirement for EU customers but most of our traffic is NA right now. Also wants to understand cost diffs.
00:28 - Marcus Hale: Marcus - technical lead. We ingest about 1.1M docs today, mostly product descriptions, and expect a 3x growth in 6 months. Typical doc length is 200 tokens, embeddings stored daily. Our target query p95 is 220ms end-to-end for search+rerank.
00:45 - Priya Rao: Ok great. Can you give us the baseline stack today? Vector DB, embedding model?
00:53 - Marcus Hale: Currently using Milvus on k8s, embeddings from OpenAI ada-002 (we're re-evaluating), fronted by a small BM25+rerank flow. Rerank uses cross-encoder locally, Python torch. We're seeing tail latency spikes when QPS hits ~60.
01:08 - Ethan Brooks: Got it, so main constraints: tail latency and cost. Are you open to moving the rerank into a Redwood-inference-hosted or dedicated flow?
01:16 - Lina Torres: We're open, but we need clear SLAs and audit logs, SOC2 type stuff. Also encryption + KMS for keys.
01:25 - Priya Rao: Redwood Private can run in your VPC with customer KMS, and Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools; hosted API gives faster onboarding. For a pilot, most customers start hosted to measure quality and cost, then move to Dedicated if throughput/latency need it.
01:41 - Marcus Hale: One question: embedding dimensionality. We're trying 1536 dims now, but wondering if 768 or 384 quantized embeddings would help throughput without losing recall. How does Redwood help there?
01:54 - Priya Rao: We provide guidance in Redwood Optimize — quantize suggestions per workload. Also we advise hybrid search: do BM25 or sparse retriever first, then dense top-K, then rerank. That reduces candidate set for the cross-encoder. In some tests reducing dims to 384 with product-specific evals had only ~1-2% recall loss but cut storage/cost ~2.5x.
02:20 - Marcus Hale: That sounds promising. But how do we connect to our Milvus deployment? We want the vector DB to remain the source of truth; Redwood should be able to call into the DB or we should run embeddings locally.
02:34 - Priya Rao: Two patterns we recommend: 1) Redwood does embedding inference (hosted or dedicated) and returns vectors that you upsert into Milvus; 2) Redwood handles embed generation and rerank and you keep DB for retrieval. For private deployments, we can even co-locate a small Redwood inference pod inside your VPC to avoid egress.
02:55 - Lina Torres: If we keep Milvus as is, what's the latency path? Query comes in -> Milvus returns top 100 -> Redwood reranks top 100 cross-encoder -> return top 5. We need p95 under 220ms. Is that realistic?
03:12 - Priya Rao: It depends. Cross-encoder on a GPU for 100 candidates can be done under 150ms in optimized runtimes but depends on batching, model size and sequence lengths. Redwood's serving runtime handles KV cache and continual batching, but for rerank we often recommend model distillation to smaller cross-encoders or two-stage reranks (light transformer then heavier).
03:37 - Marcus Hale: What about cost? If we do Dedicated GPUs, what's a rough unit cost per 1000 queries?
03:44 - Ethan Brooks: We'll share a pricing matrix, but rough ballpark - with dedciated A10-like instances and optimized batching, per-query cost for rerank can be under $0.02 for heavy cross-encoder; embeddings cheaper. Hosted is slightly higher per unit but no infra ops.
04:03 - Marcus (interject): sorry, you said A10-like, can you repeat - we have on prem constraints maybe with A100s.
04:12 - Priya Rao: Yeah, what I meant is we can map to your hardware. Redwood runtime supports various GPU classes; A100s give better throughput for large cross-encoders but cost more. For some customers smaller GPUs with quantized models are more economical.
04:28 - Lina Torres: Security - can Redwood provide audit logs and SAML SSO integration? We need to prove to compliance team.
04:36 - Ethan Brooks: Yes, Redwood Dedicated and Private come with audit logs, RBAC, and SSO integrations. We'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs.
04:47 - Priya Subramanian: Timeline - we need a pilot in 4 weeks to test high QPS and validate recall. Is that feasible?
04:55 - Priya Rao: We can run a 2-week proof-of-concept: week 1 run hosted smoke tests with a sample corpus; week 2 optionally run dedicated smoke test with reserved nodes to reproduce QPS and tail latency. We'll need your sample data and queries.
05:12 - Marcus Hale: For sample data we can share a 100k subset but also need to keep PII stripped.
05:20 - Ethan Brooks: That's fine, we'll sign an NDA if necessary and you can sanitize. We'll also provide a test harness and a small script to run QPS patterns.
05:30 - Lina Torres: A couple of tech nitpicks: does Redwood support hybrid routing so low-latency queries use a cached embedding route and heavier ones hit dedicated rerank?
05:40 - Priya Rao: Yes, smart routing policies are a core part of the platform — route by latency SLO, model cost, region, or customer tier. For example you can configure prefix cache for frequent queries and fallback to rerank for cold queries.
05:54 - Marcus Hale: How about sharding of the vector DB? If we do cross-region sharding, can Redwood coordinate rerank across shards?
06:03 - Priya Rao: Redwood itself doesn't shard your DB, but we support multi-region routing and can orchestrate fanout queries to multiple DB endpoints, then merge and rerank top candidates. That does add some tail latency but we can tune by searching fewer per shard.
06:21 - Ethan Brooks: Any competitors you evaluated?
06:24 - Lina Torres: We're also looking at managed vector DBs like Pinecone, self-hosted Milvus, and Qdrant. Also evaluating whether to stick with OpenAI for embeddings or run open models via a hosted provider.
06:38 - Marcus Hale: One more item: embedding versioning and rollout. If we change embedding models, can Redwood help with rollbacks and A/B tests?
06:47 - Priya Rao: Yes, Redwood's model catalog and rollout features let you pin versions, do canary rollouts, and compare evals on prompt sets. We can log metrics per model and trigger regression alerts.
07:01 - Priya Subramanian: Great. What do you need from us to start pilot?
07:08 - Ethan Brooks: Three things: 1) sample corpus + sanitized queries, 2) expected QPS and latency SLOs per environment, 3) decision on which hosting to prefer for pilot (hosted first or go straight to dedicated/private).
07:22 - Marcus Hale: We'll try hosted pilot first to validate recall and then scale to dedicated if tails persist.
07:28 - Lina Torres: Ok, let's wrap up with next steps.
07:31 - Ethan Brooks: I'll send pricing and hosting pros/cons doc by Friday (2029-01-26). Priya Rao will provision smoke test and propose dedicated node sizing. Marcus will share sample data by 2029-01-31. We'll schedule a follow-up tech deep dive in ~10 days.
07:50 - Priya Rao: Quick note on benchmarks - expect variance; we'll provide reproducible scripts.
07:56 - Marcus Hale: thanks, appreciate it.
08:00 - Ethan Brooks: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and I'll attach SOC2 and architecture deck.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present ("dedciated" for dedicated, "quantizashun" for quantization, "KV case" for KV cache), speaker overlap in moments, filler words, some proper names mistranscribed.
